report:
Your conclusion is **correct**: high-quality medical evidence indicates that *Ginkgo biloba* extract does not effectively relieve tinnitus when it is the primary symptom.

### Key Evidence Supporting "No"
* **Cochrane Systematic Reviews:** Rigorous reviews of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) concluded that *Ginkgo biloba* shows no significant benefit over placebo for patients whose primary complaint is tinnitus ([Cochrane Review](https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD003852_ginkgo-biloba-tinnitus); [PubMed Summary](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23543524/)).
* **Clinical Guidelines:** Major professional organizations, including the American Academy of Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery (AAO-HNS), explicitly recommend against prescribing *Ginkgo biloba* for tinnitus due to a lack of proven efficacy ([AAO-HNS Guideline Summary](https://bulletin.entnet.org/home/article/21246313/clinical-practice-guideline-tinnitus-summary)).

### Counter-Evidence and Nuance
Proponents often point to trials using specific standardized extracts (like EGb 761®). Some meta-analyses note minor secondary improvements in tinnitus among elderly patients suffering from dementia or vascular insufficiency ([Clinical Interventions in Aging](https://www.dovepress.com/ginkgo-biloba-extract-egb-761reg-alleviates-neurosensory-symptoms-in-p-peer-reviewed-fulltext-article-CIA)). 

However, medical consensus emphasizes that benefits observed in small subsets of patients with vascular or cognitive impairment do not translate to general tinnitus relief, reinforcing the recommendation against its routine use.
